title: Eigenoperator Entanglement Statistics in Local Lindbladians
authors: Ze-Kai Hong, Xu Feng, Zhi-Cheng Yang
abstract: Random matrix spectral statistics are widely used to diagnose quantum chaos in open systems, but whether chaotic eigenvalue correlations are accompanied by Haar-typical eigenoperators remains unclear. We study the operator-entanglement statistics of Liouvillian eigenoperators with near-maximal entanglement, analogous to states near the middle of the spectrum in Hamiltonian systems. Using the Kullback-Leibler divergence, we show that Haar-random statistics accurately describe both the Ginibre and class-AI$^\dagger$ Gaussian ensembles. For purely dissipative random Lindbladians, we find that locality of the jump operators drastically alters the eigenoperator-entanglement statistics. Nonlocal Lindbladians remain relatively close to Haar-random behavior, whereas local Lindbladians deviate increasingly from random-matrix statistics with system size. Moreover, unlike in Hamiltonian systems, the most highly entangled eigenoperators of local Lindbladians do not generally lie in the region of largest density of states, owing to the clustered structure of the complex eigenspectrum. We introduce an iterative $σ$-clipping scheme to extract the high-entanglement distribution without preselecting a spectral window, and find that it is Gaussian for nonlocal Lindbladians but log-normal for local ones. Remarkably, the same log-normal distribution, with no additional fitting, also describes dissipative mixed-field Ising chains belonging to distinct non-Hermitian symmetry classes. Our results therefore point to a universal eigenoperator-entanglement distribution for local Lindbladians that is not captured by generic non-Hermitian random-matrix ensembles.
summary: This work investigates how entanglement statistics of quantum operators behave in open quantum systems described by Lindbladians. By comparing local and nonlocal models, the authors find that locality imposes a distinct, universal log-normal distribution on the entanglement entropy, which is a signature not captured by generic random matrix theories.
main_problem: To characterize the operator-entanglement statistics of Liouvillian eigenoperators in open quantum systems and determine if these statistics reveal universal properties distinct from generic random matrix ensembles.
main_result: Locality in the jump operators drastically alters the eigenoperator-entanglement distribution, causing it to be log-normal for local Lindbladians, a distribution found to be universal across different non-Hermitian symmetry classes.
method: The study uses the Kullback-Leibler divergence and an iterative $\sigma$-clipping scheme to analyze the entanglement entropy distribution of eigenoperators, comparing them against Haar-random predictions.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on open quantum systems governed by Lindblad master equations, comparing random Lindbladians (local vs. nonlocal) with a physical realization: the mixed-field Ising chain.
key_observables: Operator-entanglement statistics (distribution of entanglement entropy), Kullback-Leibler divergence ($D_{KL}$), and the complex spacing ratio.
important_parameters: System size ($N$), locality of jump operators, and the nature of the random matrix ensemble (Ginibre, class-AI$\dagger$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximating the $D_{KL}$ via moment matching and using an iterative $\sigma$-clipping scheme to extract the high-entanglement asymptotic distribution.
figures_summary: Figures show the decay of $D_{KL}$ for various random ensembles, and later figures illustrate the collapse of the $\sigma$-clipped entanglement-entropy distributions onto Gaussian (nonlocal) or log-normal (local) forms.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from established diagnostics in closed systems to the complex spectral problem of open systems, first analyzing random Lindbladians to establish the effect of locality, and then applying these findings to the mixed-field Ising chain to demonstrate universality.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, entanglement-based diagnostic tool to distinguish between different physical mechanisms (e.g., locality vs. randomness) in open quantum dynamics, complementing traditional eigenvalue spacing statistics.

The main panels enlarge the dominant spectral region, while the insets in (a) and (c) show the full spectra. (a)&(c) Eigenvalues colored by the normalized spectral density ρ. FIG. 4. Finite-size collapse of the σ-clipped distributions in terms of the normalized variable of Eq. (18), for system sizes N = 4, . . . , 7. Panels (a) and (b) show the nonlocal and local ensembles, respectively. The gray shading shows the Gaussian fit in (a) and the log-normal fit in (b), both fitted to the N = 7 data; the colored lines show the numerical results for N = 4, . . . , 7. The distribution converges in both cases as the system size increases. As a comparison, in (c)&(d) we plot the raw entanglement distributions, normalized by the corresponding raw root-mean-square distance ∆0(N). The raw distribution instead shows no clear sign of convergence with system size.
